findings.message: packages/protocol/src/join.ts protocolMismatchMessage changes the server's 426 refusal text from 'Protocol version mismatch: this client speaks vX, the server speaks vY. Reload the page to update.' to 'Protocol version mismatch: client vX, server vY. Reload the page to update.'. The change serves the decisions' under-100-byte rule (the old text echoed an untrusted clientVersion of any length), and the worker disclosed it as an open assumption. It still departs from the literal acceptance that the 426 refusal keeps its exact message. The integration tests (tests/integration/match.test.ts) check it only with /Protocol version mismatch/, not the exact text that decisions.md asks integration tests to assert; only the unit test in protocol.test.ts pins the full string.
findings.requirement: the server's own 404/409/426 refusals keep their exact messages

findings.message: Residual seat squatting through joinById, as decisions.md accepts. MatchRoom.authorizeEntry passes any well-formed createToken, and any code of another live match (which anyone gets by creating their own match). So a caller who knows a roomId can have Colyseus reserve seats (Room._reserveSeat) before MatchRoom.onJoin/admit refuses them, and a caller who never opens the WebSocket holds each seat until the 15 s seatReservationTimeout. Nothing exposes roomIds to non-members: Colyseus 0.18 serves only POST /matchmake and has no listing route. docs/architecture.md records this limit. It is noted here for traceability, not as a defect.
findings.requirement: Finding 1: a private match can be neither joined nor have a seat reserved in it without its code, as the three layers in `decisions.md` require.
